No cited context makes sending every request to generation turn its output into curated CQA wording. All three passes must restart after any authored repair.

sourceReviews.supportingSummary: The comparison assigns dynamic factual context to query-time retrieval, stable style to evaluated fine-tuning and conversation preferences to prompts. It recommends adding complexity after measured need. The three-layer example is a direct responsibility allocation, not evidence of Expert-level architectural reasoning. Question-specific evidence: The comparison assigns dynamic facts to RAG and per-conversation context to prompt engineering, reserving tuning for behavior. The all-three example and prompt-plus-tuning section assign exactly these distinct concerns. The optimization spectrum separates context accuracy from trained behavior and says not every app needs all three. RAG is recommended for dynamic/frequently changing data while tuning may need retraining as requirements change.

choiceReviews.rationale: Model training is useful for stable behavior, not a substitute for these two runtime context mechanisms.
The combination is technically defensible but repeats t-010’s responsibility allocation and does not justify Expert difficulty.
Dropping the validated style mechanism and explicit preference loses requirements the stem asks to preserve.
The source-backed purpose of the training set does not make its original facts current indefinitely.

reviews.verificationNotes: Rejected after independent comparison with ai103-t-010 and SEM-012. Both assign changing facts to retrieval, style to fine-tuning and request guidance to prompts; already-evaluated style versus a measured style defect changes adoption timing, not the tested fact. The Expert label also fails: the source’s all-three list nearly supplies the answer and every distractor discards an explicit requirement. Preserve the technical manual hold and reject this duplicate hash.
